subject: Phase 4 - half A core agents: a versioned prompt library and the trace column that names it, the numbered span offering every extraction cites through, DecisionScout, DecisionStructurer, AssumptionExtractor with the estimated_as edge it writes when an assumption is an estimate in disguise, the extraction pipeline wiring all three onto phase 3's ingestion, and the evaluation harness that grades the result against the phase 3 corpus
conditions: the evaluation harness is priced as FOUR line items and not one - matching, metrics, the runner and the report renderer, roughly 550 production lines against roughly 700 test lines - because OUT-0004's whole error was the corpus generator priced in four words and delivered as five modules, and a harness with its own matching semantics is the same shape of thing

the three agents are priced separately at roughly 200, 300 and 350 production lines with test files larger than each, because the failure paths are where the lines are: a candidate that cannot be resolved to an offered span, a decision with no rejected option, an assumption whose predicate is quantified but whose work class is not usable

the prompt library is a real stored artefact with a schema migration behind it - prompt_id and prompt_sha on llm_trace - and not a dictionary of strings, so it carries a migration, a round-trip test and a packaging concern inside this estimate
three ADRs and the phase report are inside this estimate
no schema change beyond migration 004: decision, assumption, estimate, link and their CHECK constraints already exist from phase 1, and no new FindingKind member is introduced

no live API call is made and no key exists; MockProvider serves every call, which means the reported precision and recall are measurements of the plumbing and of the graders, not of a model, and the report has to say so in those words
the numbers in the metrics table are produced by praxis eval and pasted in, never typed by hand
calibration_note: No bias correction applied, for the fifth time and the same reason. Four outcomes exist in four work classes and they still disagree in direction - scaffolding over 2.3x, data-modelling under 2.1x, llm-integration under 1.24x, agent-implementation over 1.3x, n = 1 each. BiasDetective refuses to answer below n = 5; applying a factor here would be the unprincipled adjustment this product exists to replace, and it would be the author breaking his own product's rule at the first opportunity. Worth noting for the first time: this is the SECOND estimate in agent-implementation, so OUT-0005 will take that class to n = 2. Still below the threshold, still no correction - but from here one class has a history rather than a point, and the phase 8 demo gets more interesting the moment any class reaches five. The scope correction OUT-0002 asked for, OUT-0003 confirmed and OUT-0004 sharpened IS applied and is a different thing: the conditions price components rather than phases, and they count the evaluation harness as four components because the one line item OUT-0004 got badly wrong was the one described in four words.
risk_note: The largest uncertainty is not line count, it is whether the mock provider produces extractions good enough for the precision and recall figures to be about the pipeline rather than about the synthesiser. If they are dominated by the mock, the harness is still the deliverable and the report says the numbers are a floor. That is a reporting outcome, not a scope change, and it is inside this estimate.
source: docs/reports/NEXT.md and the phase 4 scope, stated on the phase branch before any praxis/prompts, praxis/agents or praxis/eval file was created

subject: Phase 5 - assumption formalization and monitoring, closing Half A: a three-valued predicate DSL (lexer, parser, evaluator, interval arithmetic, expiry conditions, world state) as deterministic code, AssumptionFormalizer populating the Phase 1 predicate and expiry_condition fields, AssumptionMonitor evaluating them and emitting AssumptionBreach findings through the Phase 1 store, deterministic blocking plus ContradictionDetector writing contradicts links, ArchaeologistAgent answering why-not-X from stored records only, corpus revision documents and a monitoring section in the answer key, and the Phase 4 eval harness extended to grade all four agents with cost per document per agent
conditions: the predicate DSL is priced as SIX line items and not one - lexer, parser, evaluator, interval arithmetic, expiry conditions and world state, roughly 900 production lines against roughly 900 test lines - because it is a parser, and OUT-0005's lesson is that an artefact described in three words is the one that comes in at 2x. Every one of those six is mostly the code that says no: an identifier nothing bound, a division by zero, a comparison between a string and a number, a quotation that never closes

the four agents are priced separately at roughly 350, 450, 400 and 350 production lines with test files at least as large, and the refusal vocabulary is priced INSIDE each one rather than assumed to be a happy path with a guard clause - this is the correction OUT-0005 bought and it is the only correction applied
praxis/monitor/ is priced as three line items - the facts file and the one hop the store itself answers, the monitor, and the breach finding - roughly 450 production lines

the corpus extension is priced as two line items and not one: a revision template that reverses a topic's assumption so the arithmetic contradiction path has a graded case, and a monitoring section in the answer key carrying facts, events and per-assumption expected status. The second bumps the ground truth FORMAT_VERSION to 2

the eval extension is priced as four line items against the four existing modules - matching, metrics, harness, report - roughly 450 production lines, and it ADDS to them rather than building a second harness. Score gains a label, metrics gains a PairScore with the same arithmetic, and report renders both into the table Phase 4 established

NO schema migration is needed and none is written: assumption.status, the four AssumptionStatus members, FindingKind.ASSUMPTION_BREACH, FindingKind.CONTRADICTION and LinkType.CONTRADICTS all exist from Phase 1, and the schema stays at version 4. If this condition turns out to be false the estimate is wrong by a migration, a round-trip test and a ledger entry
no entry is added to the ADR 0006 routing table, because all four Phase 5 agents are already in it and in praxis/config/models.py - this was checked rather than assumed

the monitor's re-runnability costs no new persistence: it evaluates always, because evaluation is arithmetic and therefore free, and writes only when the verdict changes. The formalizer skips any assumption whose predicate already parses, so a second run costs zero model calls. Neither needs a column the store does not have
four ADRs and the phase report are inside this estimate

no live API call is made and no key exists; MockProvider serves every call, which means every model-dependent number is a floor measuring the plumbing rather than a model, and the report says so in those words beneath the table - the same reporting outcome EST-0005's risk note predicted and OUT-0005 confirmed

the monitor's store-derived binding - an Outcome reaching back through estimated_as to breach the assumption a decision rests on - is built and unit-tested but binds nothing in the corpus run, because no agent writes an Outcome until Phase 6. That zero is reported as not-yet-exercised rather than as a failure
the numbers in the metrics table are praxis eval output pasted in, never typed by hand
calibration_note: No bias correction applied, for the sixth time, and this time the reason has to be stated more carefully than before because the data has changed shape. The ratios were recomputed from estimates.jsonl and outcomes.jsonl rather than recalled: scaffolding over 2.27x, data-modelling under 2.10x, llm-integration under 1.24x, agent-implementation over 1.31x, agent-implementation over 2.18x. That is five outcomes in FOUR classes, not five classes - agent-implementation is at n = 2 and both of its points are over-estimates. It is the first class in this corpus with a direction rather than a dot, and Phase 5 is a third estimate in that same class. Two points agreeing is not a bias; it is two points agreeing, and BiasDetective refuses below n = 5. Applying a factor here would be the author breaking his own product's rule at exactly the moment it first became tempting, which is the moment it matters. A third independent over-estimate in this class is worth more to the Phase 8 demo than one tuned number would be. This estimate is built bottom-up from line items at the same judgement of effort per component that EST-0005 used, and is deliberately NOT rescaled by the observed 2.18x - rescaling by measured throughput on the same work class is a bias correction wearing a different hat, and calling it a scope correction would not make it one. The scope correction IS applied and is a different thing: the conditions price components rather than phases, they price the predicate DSL as six items because it is a parser, and they price each agent's refusal vocabulary inside the agent rather than outside it, which is the one thing OUT-0005 showed every agent in Phase 4 got wrong in the same direction.
risk_note: Two risks, and they are not the line count. First: the predicate DSL is the first artefact in this project whose correctness is a grammar rather than a behaviour, and ADR 0001 assumption 1 - adr_predicates_parsed / adr_predicates_total >= 0.9 - is a predicate this phase is supposed to fire and then answer. If the hand-written ADR predicates do not parse at 0.9, that is a finding the system was designed to surface and it gets reported as one rather than fixed by widening the grammar until it passes. Second: the corpus currently contains no contradicting pair at all, so the ContradictionDetector has nothing to be graded against until the revision template exists. The corpus work is therefore a dependency of the metric and not a tidying task, and if it is cut the contradiction row in the table is unmeasurable rather than zero.
blocked_note: 24.0h, and it is the least meaningful number in this record. Blocked has been predicted twice and missed in both directions by different magnitudes - EST-0004 predicted 20.0 against an actual 12.8, EST-0005 predicted 16.0 against an actual 72.3 - because for this project blocked time is elapsed wall clock between sessions ended by credit exhaustion, which contains nights. It measures when the author slept, not when the work waited. It is logged because the Estimate record has the field and a phase with a hole in it is a hole in the Phase 12 demo, and it should be read as a prediction about session boundaries rather than about engineering.
source: The Phase 5 scope as given by the product owner, stated on branch feat/phase-5-assumption-formalization before any praxis/predicates, praxis/monitor or Phase 5 praxis/agents file was created
